name: Deno
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2017. A Chadic Cornucopia. Ed. Paul Newman. Oakland, CA: eScholarship, California Digital Library.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Deno appears only in the Bole-Tangale language list. FAMILY-LEVEL: ch. 1 p. 6 '- stress: no Chadic language has stress as a prosodic parameter'; ch. 5 p. 89 'All Chadic languages are tone languages.. prosodic amplitude in Chadic phonological systems generally is a function of the interaction of tone, syllable weight, and intonation and plays no role that is not attributable to those properties.' Nothing Deno-specific.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Luther Hon, Adedamola Aregbesola, Thelma Araokanmi, John Muniru & David Onoja. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Some Endangered West Chadic A.2 Bole Languages of Bauchi State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-011. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only published work with Deno language data: two 222-item tone-marked phonetic wordlists (Zalanga, Siri; elicited by Julius Dabet, 17 Aug 2020; Appendix F, printed p. 55ff). Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventory' (pp. 32-34) gives pooled consonant/vowel charts for seven varieties incl. Deno ('initial, cursory observations'); Appendix F p. 55: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' No mention of stress/accent (sole 'stress' hit p. 17 is the verb).

sources.citation: Zoch, Ulrike. 2014. Verbalmorphologie der Bole-Tangale-Sprachen (Nordostnigeria). (Schriften zur Afrikanistik 22.) Frankfurt: Peter Lang. Publisher preview (32 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Deno only named in Tabelle 1 (classification after Crozier & Blench 1992) and the geographic list pp. 29-30; no Deno data in the preview; nothing on Akzent/Betonung.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1978. Bole-Tangale Languages of the Bauchi Area (Northern Nigeria). (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde, Serie A, 13.) Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Deno data at all: 'Although I was not able to investigate Kubi and Deno, examination of the word lists in Gowers (1907) shows that they are closely related to each other and form a subgroup together with Gera and Geruma' (Introduction pp. 10-12). Group-level note for the languages he did record, p. 9: 'These languages all have two phonemic tones only.' No stress/accent statement anywhere in the book.
